title: Need advice - AI art generation
author: Equivalent-Hippo9905
selftext:
Hi, I am completely new to game development. It has been a journey over the past month learning about different terms and getting my game in shape. I am doing this part time since I work with AI a lot at my job, and as the capabilities got better, I wanted to apply it to my hobby. 

Ran into a big problem with the art asset. I have minimal experience with Blender and Godot, and I am terrible at artwork. So I wanted to use Claude with Blender and Godot MCP to help with creating them. But they are always not up to my standard.

It seems to work for pixel art and I see a lot of AI art generator doing that but what about more realistic type of 2D art? Online seems to call the style I am looking for as painterly or painted ink. 

Any advice will be appreciated!

comments.author: Rsouss
comments.body: Take your art example: a character, create an AI video with the movements you want, and then capture the frames from the video.

replies.author: Equivalent-Hippo9905
replies.body: Any tools that you have used successfully for this?

replies.author: Rsouss
replies.body: Yes, you can generate the video in King AI. To capture the frames, I have my own tool that I created. However, it's very simple to use. To capture the frames correctly, set the timer to 0.2 milliseconds to capture the video, and reduce the video speed to 0.50x.

comments.author: bettertagsweretaken
comments.body: Meshy and 3D AI Studio provide excellent image to mesh quality. Incredibly high poly count, though. And you still have to rig and animate it. Mixamo is free on that front, but it's a pipeline I'm not familiar with. I'm doing a game with minimal animations where VFX carry all the animation.

replies.author: Equivalent-Hippo9905
replies.body:
Thanks for the tips. I am also doing a game now with minimal animations (perhaps even none) and just using VFX but what about background art and the character art itself? I am finding it hard to get those looking good.

And for VFX any tools that you rely on?

replies.author: bettertagsweretaken
replies.body:
I'm building everything in Godot and between me, Claude, and Fable/Opus we're building out the particles. 

I have to say, the VFX systems were the ones that required me to get my hands dirtiest. I know how and why each setting in the particle systems works! That being said, Claude can and has authored some art that was almost passable on first blush. 

For the background art and stuff you need to find an output that will repair produce the same results and then generate multiple images of the target in multiple angles (for characters).

For background art, I'm lucky again, i guess. I use the art from the game itself (like the actual in-game levels as screenshots and background materials), because it's a tactics game. Anything i generate for it would be an abstraction and that's not helpful for showing people the game itself.

replies.author: Equivalent-Hippo9905
replies.body: Thanks! I will give it a go! Wish you success in your game too!

comments.author: Ok-Lengthiness-6692
comments.body: Send chatgpt some images of the style you like, ask for it to describe it for a new prompt. Then use that prompt and the source images to generate the art you want. Collect dozens of new examples you have generated and use those as references to generate more art.

replies.author: Equivalent-Hippo9905
replies.body:
I tried that and it seems to be able to analyse but it hasn't been very effective in re-creating the chatgpt mockup looks. 

Do I need to teach it anything for how to use blender etc? I fed it the blender official documentation and it got better but still not up to par

replies.author: Ok-Lengthiness-6692
replies.body: I'm not sure I understand what exactly you are trying to do. You said 2D art, but are using blender. Are there any examples of games you are trying to replicate? Or what is the goal exactly here. Blender is generally a 3D tool.
